messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] multiple testing correction for multiple trait
parts:
You should consider the number of traits analyzed when assessing QTL mapping results, but formal correction for the multiple phenotypes is seldom applied, and there's no standard method for doing so.

The following paper is an example of one approach I took:

Burrage LC, Baskin-Hill AE, Sinasac DS, Singer JB, Croniger CM, Kirby A, Kulbokas EJ, Daly MJ, Lander ES, Broman KW, Nadeau JH (2010) Genetic resistance to diet-induced obesity in chromosome substitution strains of mice. Mamm Genome 21:115-129

http://www.biostat.wisc.edu/~kbroman/publications/burrage.pdf

karl

On Apr 22, 2013, at 2:55 PM, Sai <saisri...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Dear Karl,
>
> I am currently trying to map QTL for multiple traits treating them as each trait separately as a phenotype. Permutation scheme is applied for each trait individually and the significance threshold is calculated. The genome wide significance defines the threshold for significant QTL for each phenotype trait. Is it necessary to correct for multiple testing correction if I had to compare QTLs from different traits? If yes, could you please give me overview how to go about it?
>
> Thanks a lot.
>
> Best,
> Sai
